proTips: Warm the milk first and add it gradually for a lump-free sauce.
Cook it for a full 2 minutes after it thickens so it does not taste floury.
steps: For a light sauce, whisk flour with 100 ml cold milk until smooth. Heat remaining milk with butter.
Whisk in slurry and simmer gently for 3–5 minutes, stirring thoroughly, until thick and the flour tastes cooked.
Alternatively cook flour in oil or butter for 1 minute, then whisk in milk gradually and simmer.
Season. Remove from heat before stirring in cheese if used.
summary: A smooth white sauce for pies, lasagna and vegetables, light on butter.
title: A simple white sauce with little butter

ingredients.item: fully cooked chicken and turkey mince patties
potatoes, vegetables, mustard or gravy to serve

proTips: This is a reheating method, not a recipe for raw mince.
Check your current packet.
steps: Confirm the patties are labelled fully cooked. The specific packet in the chat said fried chicken and turkey mince patties.
Heat air fryer to 180°C. Put refrigerated patties in a single layer; no added oil is usually needed.
Heat about 7–9 minutes, turning at 4 minutes. If desired, finish for 1–2 minutes at 190°C for extra colour. Ensure hot throughout; a conservative reheating target is 74°C.
Serve with sides and a little mustard or gravy.
summary: Shop-bought cooked chicken and turkey patties reheated crisp in the air fryer.
time: 7–11 min
title: Air fryer chicken and turkey patties

proTips: Frozen chips already contain some oil.
A little extra can improve browning; too much adds greasiness.
Split the batch for a small basket.
steps: Preheat air fryer to 200°C. Toss frozen chips with a very light coating of oil.
Arrange without packing the basket tightly. Cook about 18–22 minutes, shaking every 5–7 minutes, or follow the packet if its directions differ.
Cook until crisp and hot through. Salt immediately and serve.
summary: Frozen chips cooked crisp in the air fryer with a light shake halfway.
title: Air fryer frozen chips

ingredients.note: 1 large tin, or 6 Granny Smith apples, sliced and lightly stewed
up to 300 g as on Aunty Caroline's card

proTips: Chill the crumble portion of the dough for 10 minutes so it breaks into distinct nuggets.
Drain tinned apples well, or the base turns soggy.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a rectangular dish, about 22 × 30 cm.
Cream the butter and sugar. Add the flour, baking powder and salt, then the eggs last, and mix to a soft, crumbly dough.
Press about two-thirds of the dough over the base of the dish.
Spread the apples over the base. Sprinkle with the sugar, and the cinnamon, raisins and almonds if using.
Crumble the rest of the dough over the top.
Bake 40–45 minutes, until the top is golden. Serve warm with custard, cream or ice cream.
summary: A buttery crumble-dough apple tart: a pressed base, sweet apples, and more dough crumbled on top.
time: 20 min preparation plus 40–45 min baking
tips: Aunty Caroline: "I like cinnamon and raisins, even almonds, with apples."
Mom kept the same recipe in Afrikaans as "Caroline se appeltert", with her pencil note that the flour is 750 ml, level.
South African butter comes in 500 g blocks, so "½ block" is 250 g.
title: Aunty Caroline's apple tart

proTips: Smash only once, at the beginning.
Later pressing loses juices.
For double burgers use eight smaller balls and two patties per bun, retaining the same total meat.
steps: Cook bacon until crisp. Mix sauce and toast the cut buns.
Divide cold mince into four loose 110–115 g balls. Keep cold until the pan is ready. Do not knead or add egg or breadcrumbs.
Heat a heavy flat pan until very hot. Put in one or two balls and immediately press firmly into thin patties with a sturdy spatula, using a small square of baking paper if needed.
Season and leave undisturbed for 2–3 minutes to form a dark crust. Scrape firmly beneath the crust, flip and add cheese. Cook through, checking 71°C in the meat.
Build immediately with sauce, patty, bacon and pickles.
summary: Thin, crusty smashed patties with cheese, crisp bacon and a quick burger sauce.
tips: For doubles, roll 80–90 g balls and stack two thin patties per bun.
Preheat a cast iron griddle for a full 8–10 minutes on induction; smash within the first 10–15 seconds.
title: Bacon cheese smash burgers

ingredients.item: medium firm apples (Granny Smith or Pink Lady)

proTips: Spoon any caramel that leaks onto the tray back over the dumplings before dusting.
Keep egg wash off the cut pastry edges so they puff instead of gluing shut.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C conventional or 180°C fan and line a tray with baking paper.
Peel the apples and remove the cores with a corer or small knife, keeping the apples whole.
Mash the butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, nuts and salt together, then pack it firmly into each cavity.

Roll the cold pastry about 3 mm thick and cut four squares big enough to wrap an apple, about 18 cm. Sit an apple in the centre of each, bring the corners up over the top and pinch the seams closed. Cut leaves from the scraps if you like.
Chill the wrapped apples for 15 minutes. Brush thinly with egg wash.
Bake 40–45 minutes, until the pastry is deep golden and a skewer slides easily into the apple through the side.
Rest 5–10 minutes, dust with icing sugar and serve warm with vanilla ice cream.
summary: Whole apples stuffed with butter, brown sugar, cinnamon and nuts, wrapped in pastry and baked golden.
time: 30 min preparation plus 40–45 min baking
tips: Assemble earlier in the day and keep in the fridge, then bake while everyone finishes the main course.
Firm apples hold their shape when baked whole.
title: Baked apple dumplings

ingredients.item: pudding rice or short grain rice

proTips: Do not confuse a creamy loose finish with uncooked hard rice.
steps: Heat to 150°C conventional or 130°C fan. Butter a deep approximately 2 litre dish.
Mix rice, milk, cream, sugar, vanilla and salt in dish. Dot with butter and dust lightly with spice.
Bake around 1½–2 hours, stirring after 30 minutes and again later if you prefer less skin. Add hot milk if drying before rice is tender.
Finish when the rice is completely tender and the liquid is creamy; it will thicken as it stands.
Rest 10–15 minutes before serving.
summary: Creamy rice pudding baked slowly in the oven with vanilla.
time: 10 min preparation plus 1½–2 hours baking
title: Baked vanilla rice pudding

proTips: Use plain flour where possible; if substituting pizza flour, mix especially gently.
Do not wait for a centre temperature over 100°C.
steps: Heat to 175°C conventional or 160°C fan. Butter and line a standard loaf tin, approximately 23 × 13 cm.
Mash bananas, stir in butter, sugar and vanilla, then eggs and grated apple.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt and optional cinnamon separately. Fold into wet ingredients just until flour disappears.
Fill tin about two thirds to three quarters full. Bake roughly 50–60 minutes, beginning checks at 45 minutes. Tent if the top browns before the centre sets.
A skewer should show moist crumbs without raw batter. The chat also used a centre temperature around 96–98°C as a secondary check. Cool in tin 10 minutes, then on a rack 45–60 minutes.
summary: Banana bread with grated Pink Lady apple for extra moisture.
time: 15 min preparation plus 50–60 min baking
title: Banana bread with Pink Lady apple

ingredients.item: ground ginger or 5 ml finely grated fresh ginger

proTips: Do not add milk unless the batter is unusually stiff; banana, carrot and eggs provide plenty of moisture.
steps: Heat to 175°C conventional or 165°C fan. Grease and line a standard loaf tin.
Mash bananas, whisk in eggs, butter, sugar and vanilla, then stir in carrot.
Combine dry ingredients and ginger. Fold into wet mixture just until flour disappears. Keep the carrot moisture; do not squeeze it.
Transfer to tin and optionally sprinkle 5 ml sugar on top. Bake 45–55 minutes, checking from 45, until the centre has no raw batter.
Cool in tin 10–15 minutes, then on a rack.
summary: Banana loaf with grated carrot and warming ginger.
time: 15 min preparation plus 45–55 min baking
title: Banana carrot and ginger loaf

proTips: Use the spottiest banana you have and leave a few small lumps for pockets of flavour.
Cook on medium-low; the banana sugars brown faster than plain batter.
steps: Mash bananas. Mix flour, baking powder, salt and optional sugar separately.
Whisk egg, 150 ml milk, oil and vanilla, then stir in banana.
Fold wet into dry. Add milk a little at a time until thick but pourable. Rest briefly.
Cook small portions over medium heat for 1–2 minutes per side, flipping when bubbles appear and edges set. Reduce heat if browning too fast.
Serve warm with fruit, yoghurt or syrup.
summary: Fluffy flapjacks with mashed banana in the batter.
time: 10 min mixing plus 15 min frying
title: Banana flapjacks

proTips: Wholemeal flour and almond flour are not interchangeable here; use wheat flour for this version.
steps: Heat to 180°C conventional or 165°C fan and line muffin tins.
Mash bananas and whisk in eggs, melted fat, honey, milk and vanilla.
Mix flour, bicarbonate, salt and cinnamon, then fold into wet mixture. Add optional nuts or berries.
Divide among cases no more than three quarters full, add oats if desired and bake about 18–25 minutes until centres are cooked.
Cool 5 minutes in tins, then on a rack.
summary: Wholemeal banana muffins sweetened lightly with honey.
time: 15 min preparation plus 18–25 min baking
title: Banana oat muffins with modest added sweetness

puff pastry, enough to wrap without stretching

proTips: For advance preparation, fully cook chicken to 74°C, cool promptly and refrigerate; wrap and bake later until 74°C again.
Use thin bacon and check it is cooked too.
steps: For a same-day meal, season and quickly sear chicken in oil for colour. Remove to a clean plate and let surface steam subside briefly; proceed to assemble and bake immediately. Do not partially cook chicken and keep it overnight.
Brush each breast with a thin layer of BBQ sauce. Add cheese inside the edges and wrap with two thin bacon rashers.
Wrap each in cold pastry. Trim excess, seal seam underneath and cut a small vent. Remove all cling film if used to shape a cold bundle.

Egg wash and put on a lined, preheated heavy tray. Bake at 200°C conventional or 180°C fan, starting checks at 30 minutes for breasts this size. Continue until the thickest chicken centre reaches 74°C and pastry is deeply golden.
Rest 5 minutes before serving with light mash.
summary: Chicken breasts with BBQ sauce, cheese and bacon wrapped in puff pastry.
time: 30 min preparation plus cooling and 30–40 min baking
tips: Mushroom version: cook 250 g finely chopped mushrooms, 1 small grated onion, 1 garlic clove and thyme in 15 g butter until dry; cool and use a thin layer instead of BBQ sauce. Keep all filling dry.
title: BBQ bacon and cheese chicken Wellingtons

proTips: If beef needs longer, remove tender vegetables and return at the end.
steps: Season and lightly flour beef, shaking off excess. Brown in batches in oil and remove.
Soften onions; add garlic and tomato paste briefly. Deglaze with a little stock. Return beef with remaining stock, Worcestershire, thyme and bay.
Simmer very gently, covered, for about 1½–2 hours, checking liquid and stirring occasionally, until the beef is beginning to soften.
Add carrots and potatoes. Add butternut roughly 25–35 minutes before the end and courgettes 15–25 minutes before the end. Continue until beef is spoon tender and vegetables are just soft.
Uncover to reduce gravy if needed. Remove bay, adjust seasoning and garnish with parsley. Serve alone, with mash, rice or bread.
summary: Beef stew with butternut, marrows, carrots and potatoes.
time: 30 min preparation plus about 2½–3½ hours simmering
title: Beef stew with butternut and marrows

ingredients.item: Vetemjöl Special or strong bread flour
active sourdough starter at peak, assumed equal flour and water by weight
Oil or butter for the tin

proTips: Weigh the starter; do not increase it by eye.
Dough should be slightly sticky but shapeable.
steps: Use a healthy starter that has risen well after feeding. Stir 100 g starter into 300 g water, then add 500 g flour. Mix with the dough hook briefly until cohesive. Add salt and incorporate.
Cover the mixer bowl with its fitted lid. Rest 45–60 minutes. With a damp hand, lift and fold the dough from four sides. Repeat once or twice at 30–45 minute intervals if the dough needs strength.
Leave covered until visibly aerated and about 50–75 percent larger. This may take 3–6 hours or longer in a cool kitchen; use the dough, not a fixed clock.

Turn onto a lightly floured surface, form a rectangle and roll into a firm log. Put seam down in a greased loaf tin. Cover and proof until puffy and a light indentation slowly springs back, commonly 1–3 hours.
Heat fan oven to 220°C. Score a lengthwise cut about 1 cm deep. Bake 15 minutes with a small heatproof tray of boiling water below. Carefully remove steam tray and reduce to 200°C fan.
Bake 25–30 minutes more. Remove from tin; if sides or base are pale, bake directly on rack for 5 minutes. Cool on a rack for at least 1 hour, preferably longer, before cutting.
summary: The house sourdough baked in a loaf tin: 500 g flour, 300 g water, 100 g starter, 10 g salt.
time: About 7–12 hours depending on starter and room temperature
title: Bread tin sourdough

proTips: Sauce under the sponge is expected.
Test the sponge itself for raw batter without confusing it with the sauce.
This was an alternative offered before you chose buttermilk caramel.
steps: Heat to 180°C conventional or 160°C fan. Butter a deep approximately 20 cm baking dish.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt and 150 g sugar. Whisk egg, melted butter, milk and vanilla, then fold together.
Spread batter in dish. Sprinkle topping sugar evenly and dot with butter.
Pour boiling water slowly over the back of a spoon onto the surface. Do not stir.
Bake 30–35 minutes until the top sponge is set. Let stand 5–10 minutes and serve by spooning through to the sauce below.
summary: A light sponge that bakes on top of its own butterscotch sauce.
time: 15 min preparation plus 30–35 min baking
title: Butterscotch self saucing pudding

proTips: Squeeze the pineapple really well; wet pineapple makes the muffins sink.
Frost only when completely cool, and keep frosted muffins in the fridge.
steps: Heat to 175°C conventional or 160°C fan. Line muffin tins. Mix flour, sugars, raising agents, salt and spices.
Whisk oil, eggs and vanilla. Fold in dry mixture, then carrot, drained pineapple and nuts.
Fill cases no more than two thirds full. Bake about 20–25 minutes until the centres are set and a skewer shows no wet batter.
Cool 5 minutes in tins, then completely on a rack.
Beat topping butter until smooth, then briefly beat in cream cheese. Add sifted icing sugar, vanilla and optional orange zest. Chill if soft and spread on cold muffins.
summary: Carrot and pineapple muffins with cream cheese frosting.
time: 25 min preparation plus 20–25 min baking and cooling
title: Carrot cake muffins with cream cheese topping

proTips: Chicken makes this a carbonara-style meal.
steps: Mix eggs, yolks and Parmesan with plenty of pepper. Cook spaghetti in salted water, saving a mug of its water.
Cook bacon until browned. Add small chicken pieces and cook to 74°C; add garlic briefly. Drain excess fat if necessary.
Add pasta and a little hot pasta water to the pan. Remove from direct heat and let fierce sizzling subside.
Toss in egg mixture, stirring continuously and adding pasta water a spoonful at a time for a creamy coating. Keep moving so eggs do not scramble.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper. Use pasteurised eggs when keeping the sauce softly set.
summary: Chicken and bacon spaghetti in a silky egg and Parmesan sauce.
time: 30 min
title: Chicken and bacon carbonara style pasta

proTips: For the rice variation, cook 300 g rinsed rice separately and serve underneath.
Do not simply double the cooking time for a doubled batch.
steps: Heat to 180°C conventional or 160°C fan. Season and brown chicken in 30 ml oil; remove.
Add remaining oil, butter, onions, carrots and celery. Soften 5–7 minutes. Add garlic for 1 minute, then flour and cook for 1–2 minutes.
Gradually stir in wine if using and stock, scraping the pot. Return chicken and add potatoes, herbs, bay and half the lemon juice.

Cover and bake. Begin checking at 60 minutes; continue until thighs are tender, potatoes yield easily and chicken reaches 74°C. The historical recipe allowed 1½–2 hours, but boneless pieces may finish earlier.
Remove herb stalks and bay. Reduce liquid on the hob if too thin. Adjust lemon, salt and pepper and scatter parsley.
summary: Thighs, potatoes and vegetables baked in a lemony herb sauce in one pot.
time: 25 min preparation plus about 60–100 min oven cooking
title: Chicken and potato casserole

proTips: Brown the mushrooms in batches if the pan is crowded; they should squeak and colour, not steam.
A small squeeze of lemon at the end lifts the creamy sauce.
steps: Brown seasoned chicken in half the butter and reserve. Cook onion and mushrooms in remaining butter for 7–10 minutes until moisture has evaporated and mushrooms brown.
Add garlic and thyme for 30 seconds, then flour for 1 minute. Gradually add stock, followed by cream and Dijon.
Return chicken and simmer 8–10 minutes or until cooked through to 74°C and the sauce is thick. Season.
Cool promptly and chill before covering with pastry. Seal, vent and egg wash.
Bake at 200°C fan for about 25–35 minutes until deeply golden and filling reaches 74°C. Rest 5–10 minutes.
summary: Chicken thighs and browned mushrooms in a thyme and Dijon cream sauce.
time: 30 min preparation plus chilling and 25–35 min baking
title: Chicken mushroom and thyme pie

proTips: Use a star nozzle for an evenly cooking ridged shape.
Avoid trapped air in the piping bag.
Let oil recover between batches and remove all wrapping before frying.
White chocolate sauce is sweeter and needs less cream than the dark version.
steps: Bring water, butter, sugar and salt to a boil. Remove from heat, add all flour and stir firmly. Return to low heat and stir for 1 minute until a smooth ball forms.
Cool in a bowl 5–10 minutes, or paddle slowly for 2–3 minutes. Add eggs gradually until glossy, thick and pipeable; stop before the dough becomes runny. Add vanilla if using.
Pipe 10–12 cm lengths through a large star nozzle onto a lined tray. Freeze 1–2 hours until firm.
Heat oil to 175–180°C. Fry from frozen in small batches for about 4–5 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked inside. Test one first. Freshly piped churros generally take 3–4 minutes.
Drain 10–15 seconds, then roll in cinnamon sugar.
For either sauce, heat cream just to a simmer, pour over finely chopped chocolate, wait 1 minute and stir smooth. Stir in butter. Serve warm with freshly fried churros.
summary: Crisp cinnamon-sugar churros with a warm chocolate dipping sauce.
time: 25 min preparation plus 1–2 hours freezing and 15–20 min frying
title: Churros with dark or white chocolate sauce

ingredients.item: boneless fläskkarré or pork neck shoulder

proTips: Fläskkarré is pork neck or collar, not loin.
This is a juicy slicing roast; a pull-apart shoulder needs a different, much longer braise.
Never return the rested sliced roast to fierce heat.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C fan. Dry the pork. Rub with oil, mustard, garlic, herbs, salt and pepper. Sear in a hot pan for about 2 minutes per side.

Put onions, carrots and potatoes in a Dutch oven. Sit the pork on top, fat upwards. Mix stock, cider and remaining mustard; pour around the meat and add bay. Aim for 1–2 cm liquid in the pot, not a submerged roast.
Cover and cook for about 90 minutes. Check the potatoes and remove any already tender. Check the pork with a thermometer in the centre, avoiding fat seams.
Uncover and continue, checking after 20–30 minutes. For the sliceable result discussed, aim for 68–70°C in the centre. Return tender potatoes briefly to warm if removed.
Rest pork for 20 minutes. Reduce and strain the juices, skim excess fat and finish with butter. Slice across the grain.
summary: Pork neck roasted on vegetables in cider, Dijon and stock, then sliced with a glossy gravy.
time: 25 min preparation plus about 2–2½ hours cooking and 20 min rest
title: Cider and mustard pork neck roast

steps: Cook pasta in salted water just short of packet time and drain.
Melt butter, stir in flour and cook 1–2 minutes. Gradually whisk in milk, then simmer 5–8 minutes until smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon.
Remove from heat and melt in cheeses. Season, then mix with pasta. Add crisp bacon and paprika for the bacon version.
Serve straight away, or transfer to a dish and top with breadcrumbs tossed in melted butter. Bake at 190°C conventional or 170°C fan for 20–25 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Rest a few minutes before serving, with peas or broccoli alongside.
summary: Proper cheddar macaroni cheese, stovetop or baked, with a bacon option.
time: 25 min stovetop or 45–50 min baked
title: Classic macaroni cheese with bacon variation

Mix biscuit crumbs and butter and press firmly into the base.
Scatter chocolate and optional coconut or nuts. Pour condensed milk evenly over the top and add a pinch of salt.
Bake 20–25 minutes until edges are golden and the centre is set rather than liquid.
Cool completely, then chill before cutting into small bars.

time: 15 min preparation plus 20–25 min baking and cooling

proTips: For a double crust, blind bake a chilled base with weights, remove weights and dry the base before filling; a preheated baking tray helps.
steps: Fry bacon until crisp and reserve. Brown chicken in a little rendered fat; remove. Soften onion and carrots, adding a little oil only if needed. Add garlic.
Return chicken and bacon, pour in stock and simmer until carrots are tender and chicken reaches 74°C. Add peas and cream.
Stir the cornflour slurry again, add gradually and simmer until the filling is thick. You may not need all the slurry. Taste before salting.
Cool promptly, then chill fully before fitting the pastry lid. Crimp, vent and egg wash.
Bake at 200°C conventional or 180°C fan for 25–35 minutes or until pastry is deeply golden and filling is hot throughout, at 74°C. Rest 5–10 minutes.
summary: Chicken, bacon, carrots and peas in a creamy sauce under puff pastry.
time: 30 min preparation plus chilling and 25–35 min baking
title: Creamy chicken and bacon pie

ingredients.item: frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed very dry

proTips: Squeezing frozen spinach is essential.
Brown mushrooms in batches if the pan is small.
A small squeeze of lemon at the end lifts the rich filling.
steps: Soften onion in butter or oil for 4–5 minutes. Add mushrooms and cook until browned and their water has evaporated.
Add garlic for 30 seconds. Stir in squeezed spinach and fry for 1 minute to remove remaining moisture.
Add cream and simmer until creamy but not watery, about 3–4 minutes. Season and optionally add cheese.
Cool promptly and chill. Transfer to a small pie dish, cover with pastry, seal, vent and egg wash.
Bake at 200°C conventional or 180°C fan for about 25–35 minutes until puffed and deeply golden, with the filling hot throughout. Rest 5–10 minutes.
summary: Browned mushrooms and spinach in cream under a puff pastry lid.
time: 25 min preparation plus chilling and 25–35 min baking
title: Creamy mushroom and spinach pie

proTips: Drain tuna thoroughly and fold gently so it stays in flakes.
A 23 cm dish must have sufficient depth; use a larger dish rather than overfilling.
steps: Soften onion in butter for 5–7 minutes, add garlic for 30 seconds, then flour for 1 minute.
Whisk in milk gradually and simmer to a thick sauce. Add mustard, herbs, peas and sweetcorn. Cook 2–3 minutes.
Off the heat, add lemon, tuna and optional egg and cheese. Season. Cool promptly and chill fully.
Transfer to a suitably deep pie dish, cover with pastry, seal, vent and glaze.
Bake at 200°C fan for 25–35 minutes until deeply golden and filling reaches 74°C. Rest 5–10 minutes.
summary: Flaked tuna, peas and sweetcorn in a lemony white sauce under puff pastry.
time: 25 min preparation plus chilling and 25–35 min baking
tips: Your lighter 23 cm version used 280–300 g tuna, 1 onion, 150 g peas, 100 g corn, 400 ml semi skimmed milk, 30 g flour, 10 g butter, Dijon, lemon and herbs, with 150–180 g pastry for the lid and no cheese or eggs. Follow the same method.
title: Creamy tuna pie with a pastry lid

steps: Dry chicken and cut into similar pieces. Mix flour with seasoning. Set out flour, eggs and breadcrumbs in separate bowls.
Coat chicken in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing lightly. Rest coating 5 minutes.
Heat oil to 175°C. Fry a few pieces at a time for roughly 4–6 minutes, turning as needed.
Check a thick piece reaches 74°C. Drain on a rack, lightly salt and serve promptly.

ingredients.item: chicken breast fillets, cut in 3–4 cm chunks

ingredients.note: or to the fryer max line

proTips: Do not crowd the fryer. Let the oil recover to 170°C between batches or the chicken goes greasy.
Rest fried pieces on a rack, not paper, so the underside stays crisp.
steps: Pat the chicken chunks completely dry and season them with the salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder.
Mix the flour, cornflour, salt, pepper and paprika in a wide bowl. Beat the eggs with the milk in a second bowl.
Rub 15–30 ml of the egg into the flour with your fingertips to make small craggy clumps.
Dredge each chunk in flour, then egg, then back in the flour, pressing and squeezing so the coating grabs on.
Rest the coated chicken on a rack for 10–15 minutes so the coating turns tacky and sets.
Heat the oil to 170–175°C. Fry in batches for 5–7 minutes, turning, until deep golden and 74°C in the centre of a thick piece.
Drain on a rack, salt lightly while hot and serve straight away.
summary: Chunks of chicken in a double flour-and-maizena coat, deep-fried shatteringly crisp.
time: 20 min preparation plus 15 min resting and 20 min frying
tips: About 3 parts flour to 1 part cornflour: the cornflour gives the light, shattery crunch without breadcrumbs.
Season the flour as well as the chicken, or the crust tastes bland.
title: Crispy fried chicken without breadcrumbs

ingredients.item: skin on salmon fillets, 125 g each
butter, 1 crushed garlic clove and dill

proTips: Cook in batches rather than crowding seven fillets.
steps: Pat skin very dry and check for pin bones. Season just before cooking. Heat a thin film of oil in a pan over medium to medium high heat.
Place fish skin down, pressing gently for 10–15 seconds so the skin stays flat. Cook mostly on the skin side, about 4–6 minutes for these small fillets.
Flip briefly for 30–60 seconds, then continue as needed for thickness. Check the centre reaches 63°C. Add optional butter and aromatics near the end and spoon over the flesh.
Serve skin upwards with lemon, keeping sauce away from the crisp skin.
summary: Pan-fried salmon with properly crisp skin and a butter baste.
title: Crispy skin salmon fillets

proTips: Keep the cream cheese cold and stop beating as soon as it is smooth; warm or overbeaten cream cheese turns runny.
A thin crumb coat chilled for 15 minutes gives you clean, crumb-free final frosting.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Grease the 12 cm tin, line the base with baking paper and dust the sides with flour.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate, salt and all the spices together in a bowl.
In a large bowl, whisk the brown sugar and eggs for 2 minutes until pale and slightly thick. Stream in the oil while whisking, then whisk in the sour cream and vanilla.
Stir in the carrot and pineapple, then fold in the dry ingredients until just combined. A few streaks of flour are fine.

Pour half the batter into the tin and bake 28–34 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, turn out onto a rack, then re-grease and re-line the tin and bake the second half the same way. The waiting batter is fine covered at room temperature for up to an hour.

Cool both layers completely, at least 1 hour. For the frosting, beat the butter alone for 1 minute, add the cold cream cheese and beat just until smooth, then beat in the icing sugar, vanilla and lemon. Chill 15 minutes if soft.

Level any domed tops. Spread a third of the frosting on the first layer, stack the second on top, and spread a thin crumb coat all over. Chill 15 minutes, then finish with the rest of the frosting and the nuts.
summary: A tall, velvety two-layer carrot cake for a 12 cm tin, with thick cream cheese frosting.
time: 30 min preparation plus two 30-min bakes, cooling and frosting
tips: Oil, not butter, keeps the crumb moist for days. The drained pineapple adds moisture you will not taste.
Bake the layers a day ahead, wrap them well and frost on the day.
title: Double-decker carrot cake

proTips: Flaky salt sits on the surface and gives little bursts of salt rather than dissolving in.
Never fill the basket more than half; crowded chips steam instead of crisping.
steps: Peel and cut the potatoes into 1 cm chips. Rinse in cold water until it runs clear, then pat completely dry.
Fill the fryer to the max line and heat to 150°C. Fry in batches for 5–7 minutes, until cooked through but still pale.
Drain and rest on a rack for at least 10–15 minutes. You can stop here for a few hours, or freeze them.
Just before serving, heat the oil to 180–190°C and fry for 3–5 minutes until crisp and golden.
Drain, then salt immediately with flaky salt while they are hot.
summary: Deep-fryer chips the proper way: a gentle first fry, a rest, then a hot blast to crisp.
time: 20 min preparation plus about 30 min frying and resting
tips: Do the first fry ahead, then do the second fry in the last 5 minutes while the burgers finish.
Avoid waxy salad potatoes; they stay soggy.
title: Double-fried homemade chips

ingredients.item: sugar or cinnamon sugar for coating

proTips: Fry a test doughnut to set the timing.
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add warm milk and eggs and knead until cohesive. Work in soft butter and knead until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise until about doubled, around 60–90 minutes depending on warmth.
Roll about 1.5 cm thick. Cut rings or rounds and place on small baking paper squares. Cover and prove until light and puffy, around 30–45 minutes.
Heat oil to 175–180°C. Lower doughnuts carefully into oil, removing paper with tongs, and fry roughly 1½–2 minutes per side until golden and cooked inside.
Drain briefly and roll in sugar while warm. Cool before filling if making rounds.
summary: Fluffy fried yeast doughnuts rolled in sugar or cinnamon sugar.
time: 25 min preparation plus 1½–2½ hours rising and 15–20 min frying
title: Easy yeast doughnuts

proTips: Pleat the foil so the pudding has room to rise without bursting the cover.
Steam a day ahead and reheat by steaming for 1 hour; it gets darker and better.
steps: Soak the sago in the 125 ml milk for 1 hour.
Grease a 2-litre pudding basin. Put a trivet or folded cloth in a large pot with a lid and bring water to a simmer.
Mix the flour, breadcrumbs, sugar, dates and raisins in a large bowl. Stir in the soaked sago, melted butter and jam.
Mix the bicarbonate into the 45 ml milk, stir it into the bowl and mix well.
Spoon into the basin, leaving room to rise. Cover tightly with greased foil, pleated in the middle, and tie it on.
Steam for 3 hours with the water halfway up the basin, topping up with boiling water as it boils away.
For the sauce, boil the water, sugar, butter and orange peel for 5 minutes. Take off the heat and stir in the brandy.
Turn the pudding out onto a deep plate and pour some of the sauce over. Serve the rest alongside.
summary: A dark, fruity steamed pudding with sago, dates and raisins, served with a brandy syrup.
time: 30 min preparation plus 3 hours steaming
tips: Written by hand at the front of the book under "Priscilla Brokes": "Eise sê swart poeding".
A few words are faded. "Milk", "jam" and "orange peel" are best readings.
title: Eise's swart poeding

steps: Boil potatoes until tender. Meanwhile soften onion and carrot in oil, then add garlic and brown mince thoroughly.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Add stock, Worcestershire and thyme and simmer 20–25 minutes until thick, cooking mince to 71°C. Add peas and season.
Drain and steam dry potatoes, then mash with butter and warm milk.
Put filling in a baking dish. Spoon mash over, roughen with a fork and add optional Parmesan.
Bake at 200°C conventional or 180°C fan for 25–35 minutes until golden and the centre reaches 74°C. Rest 10 minutes.
summary: Beef mince and vegetables in rich gravy under buttery mash.
time: 30 min preparation plus 25–35 min baking
title: Family beef cottage pie

ingredients.item: One batch Bolognese sauce using 500 g mince, without spaghetti

proTips: Thin sauce leads to a loose lasagna.
You can assemble ahead with cooked sauces, cool promptly and refrigerate; a chilled dish may take longer.
steps: Make the Bolognese sauce and reduce until thick. Heat oven to 190°C conventional or 170°C fan.
Make béchamel: cook flour in melted butter for 1 minute, gradually whisk in milk and simmer until smooth. Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
In a deep medium baking dish, layer meat sauce, pasta and white sauce. Repeat and finish with white sauce and cheese.
Bake 40–50 minutes, covering if browning early, until pasta is tender and the centre reaches 74°C. Follow the pasta packet for any additional liquid or pre-cooking requirement.
Rest 15 minutes before cutting.
summary: Bolognese and béchamel layered and baked until bubbling.
time: 40 min preparation plus 40–50 min baking and 15 min rest
title: Family meat lasagna

ingredients.item: Water to the appropriate marked line for your rice cooker
Or about 390–420 ml water for a tightly covered hob pot

proTips: A rice cooker cup is commonly 180 ml, not the 240 ml recipe cup.
steps: Rinse rice several times until the water is less cloudy. Drain well.
For the Sakura, use its supplied rice cup consistently and the corresponding bowl line; select the long grain or white rice programme recommended by your model.
For the hob, put rice and measured water in a tight-lidded pot. Bring just to a boil, turn very low, cover and cook around 12–15 minutes until water is absorbed.
Leave covered off heat for 10 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork or rice paddle.
summary: Fluffy jasmine rice in the rice cooker or on the hob.
time: 5 min preparation plus cooker cycle or about 20 min on the hob and 10 min rest
title: Fluffy jasmine rice

proTips: Cut the roll into thick slices before pouring over the syrup for more crisp, caramelised edges.
Plain flour works, but cake flour (meelblom) gives the most tender pudding.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a long ovenproof dish.
Make the syrup first: stir the boiling water, sugar and butter until the sugar dissolves. Leave to cool slightly.
Sift the flour and baking powder together, then rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs.
Add the eggs and just enough milk to make a stiff dough.
Roll the dough out thinly on a floured surface into a rectangle and spread the jam generously over it, leaving a small border.
Roll it up from the long side like a Swiss roll and lay it seam-side down in the dish.
Pour the syrup over the roll and bake about 1 hour, until golden and cooked through. Serve hot.
summary: An old South African pudding: an apricot jam roll baked in sweet syrup until soft and saucy.
time: 25 min preparation plus about 1 hour baking
tips: Original name: Gebakte roly-poly (Kook en Geniet, p. 258). Mom's pencil notes double the batch: about 560 g flour, 4 eggs and double the syrup.
The syrup looks thin and odd going in. It is correct: it bakes into the soft sauce.
Serve with custard or a little thin cream.
title: Mom's gebakte roly-poly

proTips: Use the probe and indirect heat for a whole tenderloin.
steps: Combine marinade. Coat pork and refrigerate for 1–6 hours. Reserve any clean sauce separately before it touches raw meat.
Set up a hot direct zone and a cooler indirect zone on the grill. Lift pork from marinade, discard used marinade and pat the surface dry.
Brown on the hot zone, turning around the fillet. Move to the cooler zone to finish; whole tenderloins take longer than thin fillet slices.
Brush with BBQ sauce only in the final few minutes, turning to build a glossy coating without burning. Check the thickest part reaches 63°C, then rest at least 3 minutes, preferably 5–8.
Slice across the grain and serve with potatoes or slaw.
summary: Marinated pork fillet browned on the grill and glazed with BBQ sauce at the very end.
time: 15 min preparation plus 1–6 hours marinating and roughly 15–25 min grilling
title: Grilled pork fillet with late BBQ glaze

ingredients.item: extra egg and 15 ml milk for glazing

proTips: Use a generously sized tin; the full dough is over 1 kg.
An optional lengthwise slash gives controlled expansion.
steps: Mix and knead exactly as for the hybrid buns: combine milk, starter, sugar, yeast, flour, salt and eggs, then gradually knead in butter until smooth and elastic.
Cover in the mixer bowl and let rise around 3–4 hours until puffy.
Gently press into a rectangle, fold sides towards the centre and roll into a log. Seal seam and place seam down in a greased loaf tin.
Proof covered for 60–90 minutes or until well risen. Leave enough space for expansion; use two tins if your loaf tin is small.
Egg wash. Bake at 180°C fan for approximately 30–40 minutes, loosely tenting if needed. A centre temperature around 93–95°C and a firm structure support the doneness check.
Brush with butter, leave in tin 10 minutes, then cool on a rack for at least 1 hour.
summary: The brioche bun dough baked as a soft, golden sandwich loaf.
time: Same mixing and first rise as buns plus 60–90 min proof and 30–40 min baking
title: Hybrid brioche loaf

ingredients.item: extra egg and 15 ml milk for glaze
A little melted butter to finish

proTips: Keep the formula consistent.
The small yeast addition helps an enriched dough rise reliably while retaining starter flavour.
Follow your mixer manual for safe kneading speeds.
steps: Stir milk, starter, sugar and yeast in the mixer bowl. Add flour, salt and eggs. Mix with dough hook on low for 3–4 minutes.
Add soft butter a cube at a time. Knead on a moderate low setting for 8–10 minutes until smooth, elastic and slightly tacky. Pause if the mixer or dough becomes hot.
Leave in the mixer bowl with its fitted lid for around 3–4 hours, until about 50–75 percent larger and puffy.
Divide into 8–10 equal pieces and round into tight balls. Put in lightly oiled silicone moulds or on a lined tray. Cover and proof 60–90 minutes until noticeably puffy.
Brush with egg beaten with milk. Bake one shelf below the middle at 190°C fan for about 15–18 minutes. Tent lightly if browning too fast.
Brush lightly with melted butter, cover loosely with a clean towel for 10 minutes, then cool on a rack.
summary: Soft, rich burger buns made with sourdough starter plus a little yeast.
time: 25 min mixing plus 3–4 hours first rise, 60–90 min second rise and 15–18 min baking
title: Hybrid brioche sourdough buns

ingredients.item: brown sugar and 5 ml balsamic or Worcestershire

proTips: Low heat and time develop sweetness.
Sugar cannot substitute for the slow cooking.
steps: Heat oil and butter over medium low heat. Add onions and salt, stir and cook gently.
Stir every few minutes for 30–40 minutes. Add a splash of water to loosen browned patches before they burn.
When deeply golden and soft, taste. Add optional sugar only if needed and a small splash of vinegar or Worcestershire.
Cook 2–5 minutes more until glossy and spoon onto burgers.
summary: Slow-cooked sweet, soft onions to pile on burgers.
title: Jammy onions for burgers

proTips: Proper beaten whites are essential; a hand mixer or whisk is far more reliable than shaking a jar.
steps: Whisk yolks, milk and vanilla, then fold in flour and baking powder.
In a clean grease-free bowl, beat whites with lemon juice until foamy. Gradually add sugar and whip to firm glossy peaks.
Fold a little meringue into yolk batter, then gently fold in the rest without knocking out the air.
Heat a lightly oiled lidded nonstick pan over very low heat. Spoon or pipe tall mounds, add a little water away from the pancakes and cover.
Cook 5–7 minutes, gently turn and cook covered another 4–6 minutes until set through. Serve immediately.
summary: Tall, wobbly Japanese pancakes made with whipped egg whites.
title: Japanese style soufflé pancakes

ingredients.item: large apple, peeled and coarsely grated

proTips: Avoid beating after flour is added.
For the custard-filled suggestion, use about 5 ml of thick, chilled pastry cream covered by batter and allow extra baking time as needed.
steps: Heat to 200°C conventional or 180°C fan. Line a 12-hole muffin tin. Mash bananas and keep grated apple with its juice.
Whisk eggs, butter, sugars, yoghurt and vanilla. Stir in fruit.
Combine flour, raising agents, cinnamon and salt. Fold into wet mixture just until no dry flour remains. Add nuts if using.
Fill cases around three quarters full, using extra cases if needed. Bake 17–23 minutes, checking at 17, until centres are set with moist crumbs.
Rest 5–10 minutes in tin, then cool on a rack.
summary: Moist muffins with banana, grated apple and yoghurt.
time: 15 min preparation plus 17–23 min baking
title: Juicy banana and apple muffins

proTips: Thickness matters more than weight.
For a stronger crust another time, sear for 2 minutes per side and finish in the oven for approximately 6–10 minutes.
steps: Heat to 200°C conventional or 180°C fan. Pat chops dry. Mix oil, spices, herbs and seasoning and rub over both sides.
Arrange with space between chops. Bake for 18–22 minutes, or around 22–25 minutes for thicker chops, turning once.
If using glaze, brush on during the final 3–5 minutes. Watch closely for scorching.
Measure in the thickest meat, away from the bone. Reach at least 63°C and rest for at least 3 minutes; allow 5–10 minutes before serving.
summary: Spice-rubbed chops baked without searing, with an optional sticky BBQ-honey glaze.
time: 10 min preparation plus 18–25 min baking and 5–10 min rest
title: Juicy oven baked pork chops

ingredients.item: thin pork cutlets, about 150 g each

proTips: Knäckebröd browns quickly; lower heat if needed.
steps: Flatten cutlets evenly to roughly 5 mm and dry. Season. Whisk flour and water into a smooth coating slurry.
Dust meat lightly with flour, dip in slurry and press into finely crushed knäckebröd.
Heat oil and butter over medium heat. Fry in batches, turning carefully, until crisp and cooked through; expect around 3–4 minutes per side for thin cutlets.
Verify 63°C in intact pork and rest at least 3 minutes. Serve with lemon.
summary: Pork schnitzel coated in crushed knäckebröd with a flour slurry instead of egg.
time: 25 min
title: Knäckebröd schnitzel without egg

proTips: For substitute buttermilk use 30 ml lemon juice topped up to 480 ml with milk and stand 5–10 minutes.
Do not use concentrated Swedish ättika at the same quantity as ordinary table vinegar.
steps: Heat to 180°C conventional or 170°C fan. Butter a roughly 30 × 22 cm deep baking dish.
Beat sugar and eggs until pale. Mix in melted butter, buttermilk and vanilla.
Combine flour, bicarbonate and salt, then gently fold into wet mixture. Pour into dish, leaving expansion space.
Bake 30–45 minutes, checking from 30. If the top colours too quickly, tent with foil and reduce fan heat to 160°C. Finish when the centre is springy with no liquid batter.
Simmer sauce ingredients gently for 5–7 minutes. Pierce the hot cooked pudding and pour hot sauce over slowly. Leave 10–15 minutes to soak.
summary: A big, saucy buttermilk sponge soaked in caramel cream.
time: 20 min preparation plus 30–45 min baking and 15 min soaking
title: Large buttermilk caramel pudding

ingredients.note: or a few drops of white vinegar

proTips: Wipe the bowl and whisk with a little lemon juice before whisking the whites; any trace of fat stops them peaking.
Rub a little meringue between your fingers before it goes on. If it feels gritty, keep whisking until the sugar has dissolved, or it will weep syrup.
Dip the knife in hot water and wipe it between slices for clean cuts through the meringue.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Mix the crushed biscuits with the melted butter and press firmly over the base and up the sides of a 23 cm pie dish, packing it tight with the bottom of a glass. Bake 10 minutes and cool completely.

Turn the oven down to 150°C fan. Whisk the condensed milk, yolks, lemon juice and zest until smooth; it thickens slightly as the acid works. Pour into the cooled base and bake 15 minutes, until just set with a slight wobble. Cool for 10 minutes only, so the filling is still warm for the meringue.

Turn the oven down to 140°C fan. In a spotless bowl, whisk the egg whites with the cream of tartar until foamy. On high speed, add the sugar about 15 ml at a time, then whisk until stiff, glossy peaks form and the sugar has dissolved. Whisk in the vanilla.
Spread the meringue over the warm filling, sealing it right to the biscuit edge so it does not shrink, then pull up tall peaks with the back of a spoon.
Bake at 140°C fan for 15–20 minutes without opening the door for the first 15. It is done when the peaks are golden and the tips feel dry.
Cool uncovered at room temperature for 1½–2 hours before slicing, then refrigerate. Make it the day before for the cleanest slices.
summary: Crunchy digestive base, a tangy condensed-milk lemon filling and tall golden meringue peaks.
time: 40 min preparation plus about 45 min baking and 2 hours cooling
tips: This oven runs hot: at 170°C fan the meringue browned in 5–6 minutes, so 140°C fan is the setting that works here.
You will have exactly 4 yolks spare from the meringue whites: 3 go in the filling.
title: South African lemon meringue pie

ingredients.item: sugar, or 200 g for the original sweeter version

proTips: Less sugar changes the shiny crust and chew as well as sweetness.
Avoid overbaking while waiting for a dry skewer.
steps: Heat to 175°C conventional or 160°C fan. Line a small 20–23 cm square tin; the smaller tin gives thicker brownies.
Whisk butter, sugar, eggs and vanilla. Combine cocoa, flour, salt and baking powder separately.
Fold dry into wet just until smooth. Spread into tin.
Bake around 20–25 minutes, checking early for a thin batch. Edges should be set and the centre should have moist crumbs, without raw batter.
Cool before cutting, then warm portions briefly to serve with vanilla ice cream.
summary: Fudgy brownies, deliberately less sweet so they pair with ice cream.
time: 10 min preparation plus 20–25 min baking
title: Less sweet chocolate brownies for ice cream

proTips: Do not use a blender or food processor; it can make potato mash gluey.
Use a tea towel or fork to handle hot skin-on potatoes.
steps: Wash potatoes and cook whole or in even large pieces in lightly salted water until tender right through.
Drain thoroughly and let steam escape for 2–3 minutes. Peel while still hot if cooked in skins.
Rice or mash while hot. Fold in butter first, then add warm milk gradually until the texture suits you.
Season and serve promptly. If holding briefly, cover over gentle warmth and loosen with a little warm milk before serving.
summary: Fluffy mash made light with warm milk and only a little butter.
tips: In the stand mixer: flat beater on low, warm butter first, then warm milk gradually. Stop as soon as it is smooth.
title: Light creamy mashed potatoes

ingredients.item: sunflower oil, plus a little for the pan

proTips: The vinegar keeps the pancakes tender; you will not taste it.
If the batter thickens while it stands, whisk in a splash of water. It should pour like single cream.
steps: Whisk the water, eggs, oil and vinegar together.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a large bowl. Whisk in the liquid gradually until the batter is smooth and thin.
Leave the batter to rest for 30 minutes.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat and wipe it with a little oil. Pour in just enough batter to coat the base thinly, swirling the pan.
Fry until the edges lift and the underside is golden, then flip and cook the other side briefly.
Mix the sugar and cinnamon. Sprinkle each pancake, add a squeeze of lemon if you like, and roll it up.
summary: The big-batch South African pancake batter with a dash of vinegar, rolled up with cinnamon sugar.
time: 10 min mixing plus 30 min rest and about 45 min frying
tips: Written by hand on the title page of Mom's Kook en Geniet.
Mom also multiplied the printed pannekoek recipe by four and swapped the milk for water with a spoon of oil. Linda's batter is the same idea.
Keep the pancakes warm on a plate over a pot of simmering water, covered with a lid.
title: Linda's pannekoek

ingredients.item: tender roasting beef such as sirloin or topside, not chuck

proTips: Högrev needs the separate long braise recipe instead of this roast treatment.
steps: Heat to 220°C conventional or 200°C fan. Dry and season beef, rub with oil and sit on onion and herbs in a roasting tin.
Roast 15 minutes, then reduce to 160°C conventional or 145°C fan. Continue, beginning probe checks after another 40 minutes.

For your medium-well preference aim around 65–68°C before resting, depending on carryover; reach at least the 63°C whole-cut minimum with a 3-minute rest. Rest a joint about 20 minutes, loosely covered.
For gravy, remove excess fat, stir flour into tin juices and cook briefly on the hob. Whisk in stock, scrape browned bits and simmer until thick. Strain and finish with optional butter.
Slice thinly across the grain and serve with roast potatoes.
summary: A tender beef joint roasted to medium-well with proper pan gravy.
time: 20 min preparation plus roughly 60–90 min roasting and 20 min rest
title: Medium well roast beef and gravy

proTips: Spoon the batter in separate dollops so the syrup bubbles up between them and caramelises at the edges.
Use a dish where the syrup only comes a third of the way up; the pudding rises a lot.
steps: Boil the water, sugar and vinegar together for 5 minutes, then leave the syrup to cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a large ovenproof dish, about 25 × 30 cm.
Cream the butter and sugar, then beat in the eggs.
Sift the flour, bicarbonate, ginger, nutmeg and salt together and stir them in. Stir in the apricot jam and mix well.
Pour the cooled syrup into the dish and drop the batter into it in spoonfuls.
Bake 30–40 minutes, until the pudding is a deep golden brown and a skewer comes out clean.
Serve warm with custard or a little thin cream.
summary: Vinegar pudding: a gingery apricot sponge baked in a sweet-sour syrup until sticky and golden.
time: 20 min preparation plus 30–40 min baking
tips: Original name: Asynpoeding (Kook en Geniet, p. 258).
In Sweden use vinäger (about 5%). If you only have 12% ättika, use 50 ml topped up to 125 ml with water.
title: Mom's asynpoeding

proTips: Use bread a day or two old; fresh bread turns gluey.
Stand the dish in a roasting tin of hot water for an extra-silky custard.
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs in the warm milk and leave to cool.
Heat the oven to 160°C and grease a large ovenproof dish, about 25 × 30 cm.
Whisk the eggs and sugar together, then add the melted butter, salt and vanilla.
Stir this into the bread and milk, mix and pour into the dish.
Bake about 1 hour, until set in the middle and golden on top. The doubled batch may need 10–15 minutes more.
For the jam syrup, stir the jam into the boiling water until smooth. Serve the pudding warm with the syrup.
summary: Old-fashioned baked bread pudding, made in Mom's doubled quantity, with jam syrup.
time: 20 min preparation plus about 1 hour baking
tips: Mom wrote "×2" next to the recipe and doubled every quantity in pen. This is her doubled version.
Currant pudding: add about 300 g currants. Whisk the egg whites stiff with 45 ml sugar and spread over after 30 minutes, then bake until the meringue is light brown.
Caramel pudding: use 300 g sugar and caramelise it in a pan, then dissolve it in the milk before pouring it over the crumbs.
Coffee pudding: heat the milk with 60 ml ground coffee and strain it.
title: Mom's broodpoeding

proTips: Mix with wet hands and stop as soon as it comes together; overworked mince turns dense.
Leave room between the frikkadelle so they brown rather than steam.
steps: Mince the beef, suet and onion together.
Add the salt, pepper, nutmeg, coriander, vinegar and beaten egg.
Soak the bread in the milk, mash it fine and add the sugar.
Mix the bread and meat mixtures together well.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Shape 10–12 round frikkadelle and roll each one lightly in flour.
Pack them in a greased ovenproof dish, put a knob of butter on each and pour in the boiling water.
Bake 1–1½ hours, until browned and cooked through (71°C in the centre).
Spoon the pan liquid over the frikkadelle from time to time, topping up with boiling water if the dish dries out.
summary: Oven-baked South African meatballs, made the way Mom marked them up: with egg, soaked bread, onion and milk.
time: 25 min preparation plus 1–1½ hours baking
tips: Mom marked "things to add" next to the recipe: the egg, the slice of bread, the sugar, the onion and the milk. Keep them all in.
She circled the 60 ml of boiling water, the 1½ hours and 180°C.
Serve with mash, rice or yellow rice and the pan gravy.
title: Mom's frikkadelle

ingredients.item: cake flour or plain flour, sifted

proTips: Whisk the whites first: a clean whisk gives the most volume, and the yolks do not mind a little white on it.
Fold with a large spatula in figure-of-eight strokes so the batter keeps its air.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease a ring tin or a flat cake tin.
Sift the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt together.
Whisk the egg whites stiff with a clean whisk, then whisk the yolks in a second bowl. No need to wash the whisk in between.
Mix the melted butter and essence into the milk, then mix that with the yolks.
Add the liquid to the dry ingredients and mix for about 2 minutes.
Fold the beaten egg whites in gently, until no white streaks remain. Pour into the tin.
Bake about 35 minutes, until golden and springy.
Meanwhile make the sauce: melt the butter and brown sugar together, stir in the cream and salt, and simmer 3–4 minutes until glossy.
Serve the pudding warm with the caramel sauce poured over.
summary: A light baked sponge pudding, made with whipped egg whites and served with warm caramel sauce.
time: 20 min preparation plus 35 min baking
tips: Original name: Gebakte koekpoeding (Kook en Geniet, p. 259).
Mom's book sends you to a caramel sauce on p. 288, which is not in the photos. The sauce here is a stand-in; swap in hers if the page turns up.
title: Mom's gebakte koekpoeding

proTips: Add icing sugar a spoonful at a time at the end; a few grams separates pourable from spreadable.
steps: Coffee icing: melt the butter in the warm coffee. Add the vanilla and enough icing sugar to make an icing that spreads easily.
Orange icing: mix the cream cheese, orange juice and zest. Add the icing sugar gradually and mix well. It ices one ginger cake or 16 ginger biscuits.
summary: Two quick icings from Mom's book: a coffee icing, and an orange cream cheese icing for ginger cake.
time: 10 min
tips: From Kook en Geniet, p. 352.
Coconut icing: add 20 g fine desiccated coconut to a plain icing and sprinkle a thick layer over the top while it is still wet.
Marshmallow icing: cut 20 marshmallows into small cubes and fold them through until the icing holds its shape.

ingredients.note: about; add enough for a soft dough

proTips: Pack the balls tightly so they rise upward and bake into tall, even rusks.
steps: Sift all the dry ingredients together twice.
Rub the butter in with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Mix to a soft dough with the buttermilk.
Heat the oven to 220°C. Roll the dough into balls and pack them tightly against each other on a greased baking tray.
Bake 25–30 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
As soon as they have cooled a little, break into pieces and dry in a 100–120°C oven overnight, with the door slightly open.
summary: Big-batch buttermilk rusks, rubbed together by hand and dried until crisp.
time: 30 min preparation, 30 min baking, then drying overnight
tips: Original name: Karringmelkbeskuit II (Kook en Geniet, p. 306).

The book's notes: use less sugar or none if you prefer; for coarse rusks use half wholemeal flour; whisked filmjölk works instead of buttermilk; add 15 ml aniseed; halve the recipe for a smaller batch.
Melting the butter and adding it with the buttermilk gives a finer texture.
title: Mom's karringmelkbeskuit

Rub half of it all over the meat, under the skin too for chicken, before it goes into the oven.
Baste with the rest during roasting, spooning the pan juices back over.

time: 10 min
tips: Jotted on the title page of Mom's book under Linda's pannekoek. The handwriting is hard to read: "honey" and "basil leaf" are best guesses.
Half the amount is plenty for a whole chicken.

ingredients.item: butter and golden syrup or honey, to serve

proTips: Use a jug to pour so every plaatkoekie is the same size.
Wipe the pan with a little fat between batches and keep the heat at medium, or the outsides brown before the middles cook.
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar together. Add half the milk and the melted butter.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together and add to the egg mixture.
Add the rest of the milk gradually to make a smooth batter. Do not stir again once everything is mixed.
Heat a greased griddle or heavy pan. It is hot enough when a faint blue haze rises from the fat.
Drop spoonfuls of batter onto the pan. When the tops are full of bubbles, flip them with a palette knife and cook the other side until golden.
Serve with butter and syrup or honey.
summary: Little South African griddle crumpets, served with butter and golden syrup or honey.
time: 10 min mixing plus about 25 min cooking
tips: Original name: Plaatkoekies (Kook en Geniet, p. 307).
title: Mom's plaatkoekies

proTips: Warm the jam slightly so it spreads without tearing the sponge.
Seal the meringue to the edge of the dish so it does not shrink back.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and grease an ovenproof dish of about 20 × 20 cm.
Mix the butter, sugar, flour, baking powder, salt, egg yolks and about 60 ml of the milk into a smooth batter, as for a butter cake.
Spread the batter in the dish and bake about 30 minutes, until cooked through and golden.
Take it out and pour the rest of the cold milk over the hot sponge. Spread the jam over the top.
Whisk the egg whites stiff, then whisk in the caster sugar until glossy. Spread over the jam right to the edges.
Return to the oven for 10–15 minutes, until the meringue is golden brown. Serve warm.
summary: Leap-year pudding: a soft butter sponge soaked in cold milk, spread with jam and baked under meringue.
time: 20 min preparation plus about 45 min baking
tips: Original name: Skrikkeljaarpoeding (Kook en Geniet, p. 259).
The cold milk soaks into the hot sponge and turns the bottom into a soft, custardy layer.
title: Mom's skrikkeljaarpoeding

proTips: Breaking rather than cutting gives the rough edges that soak up coffee.
Dry them low and slow; too hot and they brown before the centres dry.
steps: Cut the butter into small pieces and add it to the milk with the sugar and salt. Heat, stirring, until the butter has melted. Cool to lukewarm.
Stir in the oil, beaten eggs and vinegar.
Sift the self-raising flour and cream of tartar into a large bowl. Stir in the lukewarm milk mixture.
Mix and knead for about 10 minutes, until the dough is smooth. The stand mixer with the dough hook does this well.
Heat the oven to 190°C. Roll the dough into balls the size of a small egg and pack them tightly against each other in greased loaf tins.
Bake 45 minutes to 1 hour, until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Turn out and, while still warm, break into rusks along the balls. Do not cut them with a knife.
Dry on racks in a 100–120°C oven for 6–8 hours or overnight, with the door slightly open so the steam escapes, until completely dry.
summary: Classic milk rusks: baked in tins, broken into fingers and dried slowly for dunking in coffee.
time: 30 min preparation, 1 hour baking, then drying overnight
tips: Original name: Soetmelkbeskuit (Kook en Geniet, p. 306–307). The recipe runs over the page break.
No self-raising flour? Use 2 kg plain flour with 105 ml baking powder and 5 ml extra salt.
Store in an airtight tin for weeks.
title: Mom's soetmelkbeskuit

proTips: Chill the soaked pork in the fridge rather than on the counter, and reheat until piping hot.
steps: Season the pork cubes lightly with salt and pepper and roll them in flour.
Fry in hot oil in batches until browned all over. Return everything to the pan, add a splash of water, cover and let it cook gently until tender, 1–1½ hours.
For the sauce, soften the onion and green pepper in a little oil for 3 minutes. Add the pineapple with its juice, vinegar, sugar, tomato sauce and soy, and bring to the boil.
Stir in the cornflour mixture and simmer until glossy and thickened.
Pour the sauce over the pork and leave it for a couple of hours so the meat takes on the flavour.
Reheat thoroughly before serving, with rice.
summary: Floured pork pieces fried, cooked tender and left to soak in a sweet-and-sour sauce with pineapple.
time: 20 min preparation, 1–1½ hours cooking plus a couple of hours soaking
tips: The page is cut off above the ingredients, so Mom's title is missing. The method is from her book.
Her book points to a sweet-and-sour sauce on p. 129 that is not in the photos. The sauce here is a stand-in.

steps: Mince the beef and pork fat together.
Add all the other ingredients and knead well, until the spices are evenly through the meat.
Shape into 10–12 flat patties and chill for 30 minutes so they hold together.
Fry in a hot pan or on the braai for 4–5 minutes a side, until browned and 71°C in the centre.
summary: Boerewors-spiced beef and pork patties with cloves, coriander and nutmeg, fried or braaied.
time: 20 min preparation plus 30 min chilling and 10 min cooking
tips: Original name: Worsfrikkadelle (Kook en Geniet). The book stops after "knead well"; the shaping and cooking are filled in.
Toast whole coriander in a dry pan and grind it for the most boerewors-like flavour.

ingredients.item: smooth cottage cheese or blended keso
tins black cherries in syrup, with their liquid

proTips: Soak the biscuits evenly but lightly; they should be moist, not swimming in sherry.
Make it the day before so the filling sets firm and the flavours meld.
Let the cherry glaze cool until just warm before pouring, so it does not melt the filling.
steps: Read the quantity note before shopping. Drain cherries and keep all liquid. Coarsely crush biscuits into a serving dish and moisten evenly with sherry.
Mix yoghurt, sugar and smooth cottage cheese. Separately whisk cream with the instant pudding until thick, following the original dry-powder mixing method only if your chosen product is suitable.
Fold the cream mixture into the cheese mixture and spread over biscuits.
Mix custard powder smooth with a little cold cherry liquid. Heat remaining liquid, whisk in slurry and cook gently until glossy and thickened.
Pour glaze over filling, decorate with cherries and refrigerate until fully set, at least 4–6 hours or overnight.
summary: The family no-bake cheesecake: sherry-soaked biscuits, creamy filling and a black cherry glaze.
time: 30 min preparation plus at least 4–6 hours chilling
tips: Package sizes are best estimates. Note your actual packets the next time you make it so the family version is exact.
Use smooth cottage cheese or blend keso until smooth, and instant (no-cook) pudding powder, not cooked custard powder, for the filling.
title: Mrs Webber cherry and sherry cheesecake

proTips: Separate trays avoid the potatoes sitting in chicken juices.
Give both trays breathing room and rotate if your oven cooks unevenly.
steps: Heat to 220°C conventional or 200°C fan. Dry drumsticks and coat with oil, paprika, garlic, onion powder and seasoning.
Arrange on a rack over a roasting tray. Toss dry potato wedges with their oil, rosemary, garlic and seasoning on a separate tray in a single layer.
Roast chicken for about 35–45 minutes, turning once. Roast potatoes alongside for 30–40 minutes, turning when browned underneath.
Check chicken reaches at least 74°C away from the bone; legs can be cooked a little further for a softer texture. Rest 5 minutes and salt potatoes while hot.
summary: Paprika drumsticks and crisp rosemary wedges roasted side by side on separate trays.
time: 15 min preparation plus 35–45 min roasting

Serve chilled in small portions.

ingredients.item: egg beaten with 15 ml milk or cream
frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed very dry

proTips: The three fillings make much more than one 500 g pastry batch; prepare extra sheets or freeze leftover filling.
Use distinct vents or seeds to identify flavours.
Cold, dry filling prevents leaks and soggy pastry.
servesLabel: About 12–16 per 500 g pastry, depending on cutter
steps: Choose one filling, or make all three with extra pastry. Mix ham filling cold. For beef, soften onion in oil, add garlic, brown mince, then spices, tomato paste and Worcestershire. Cook until almost dry and mince reaches 71°C; cool and chill.
For spinach, thaw, squeeze extremely dry and briefly fry with garlic to evaporate moisture. Cool and mix with crumbled feta, mozzarella, nutmeg and pepper.

Cut cold pastry into 10–12 cm circles. Put about 15–30 ml cold filling on one side, keeping the rim clear. Brush the rim lightly with egg, fold and press firmly. Crimp with a fork and cut a tiny vent.
Chill 20 minutes or freeze on a lined tray until firm. Apply one or two thin egg washes, chilling 5–10 minutes between coats. Keep egg off exposed pastry edges.
Bake at 200°C fan or 220°C conventional for about 20–25 minutes chilled, or 25–30 minutes from frozen. Continue until deeply golden and the filling is hot through. Rest 5 minutes.
summary: Puff pastry half-moons with beef, ham-and-cheese or spinach-and-feta filling.
time: 30–45 min preparation plus chilling and 20–30 min baking
title: Puff pastry empanadas in three flavours

ingredients.item: beef stock, plus more if needed

proTips: Tenderness decides the finish.
A chuck roast can be fully cooked yet still tough until its collagen has softened.
Keep the simmer gentle and rest the meat in a little of its liquid.
Make a day ahead for easier fat removal.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C conventional or 140°C fan. Pat the beef dry and season. Heat the oil in a heavy, lidded Dutch oven and brown the beef on all sides, allowing 3–4 minutes on the broad sides. Lift out.
Soften onions and carrots for 5 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute. Pour in stock, scraping the browned base. Add Worcestershire, bay and herbs.
Return beef. Liquid should reach halfway to two thirds up the meat; adjust for your pot. Cover and braise gently. Check liquid occasionally and top up with hot stock if needed.
Add small whole or halved potatoes for the final 75–90 minutes. Begin checking the beef after about 4½ hours. Continue in 30-minute intervals until a fork twists easily and the fibres separate.

Lift out meat and potatoes. Rest covered while reducing the cooking liquid on the hob for 10–20 minutes. Skim excess fat, strain if desired and whisk in cold butter off the heat. Season and spoon over the beef.
summary: Beef chuck braised low and slow until it pulls apart, with potatoes cooked in the gravy.
time: 30 min preparation plus 4½–5½ hours cooking
title: Pull apart braised beef with potatoes

ingredients.item: cinnamon and 5 ml sugar for the top

proTips: Grate the apple straight into the bowl so none of its juice is lost.
Check with a skewer from 25 minutes; small cakes go from moist to dry quickly.
steps: Heat to 180°C conventional or 170°C fan. Grease and line a 15–18 cm round tin.
Whisk eggs and sugar for 1–2 minutes. Add banana, apple with its juice, oil and vanilla sugar.
Fold in flour, baking powder, salt and optional cinnamon. Stop as soon as combined.
Pour into tin, keeping below three quarters full, and add optional cinnamon sugar. Bake for 25–35 minutes, checking at 25. Continue until no wet batter remains.
Rest in tin 10 minutes before turning out. Serve slightly warm with custard.
summary: A small quick cake of mashed banana and grated apple.
time: 10 min preparation plus 25–35 min baking
title: Quick small apple and banana cake

proTips: Bake one test cookie first; add 15 ml flour if the dough spreads excessively.
steps: Mix flour, bicarbonate and salt. Stir butter and sugars, then egg and vanilla. Fold in dry ingredients, then chocolate.
Chill 30 minutes so the soft dough is easier to portion. Heat to 175°C conventional or 160°C fan.
Scoop 15 ml portions onto lined trays, leaving at least 5 cm between them.
Bake 10–12 minutes until edges are golden and centres have set but remain soft. Cool on tray 5 minutes, then rack.
summary: Chewy chocolate chip cookies with about a third less sugar.
time: 15 min preparation plus 30 min chilling and 10–12 min baking
title: Reduced-sugar chocolate chip cookies

ingredients.item: A little butter or oil for bowl

proTips: Do not assume Keep Warm can finish a raw centre.
steps: Mash bananas. Whisk in eggs, yoghurt and vanilla. Stir in grated apple if following your later version.
Combine flour, oats, baking powder, optional bicarbonate, cinnamon and salt. Fold into wet mixture without beating. Batter should be thick and spoonable.
Grease the Yum Asia Sakura bowl and add batter, staying within the appliance Cake programme capacity. Do not exceed a sensible half-bowl fill.
Run the Cake programme. At completion check the centre with a skewer; if raw batter remains, continue in 10–20 minute intervals according to your model controls.
Leave in the switched-off bowl for 10 minutes, then turn out and cool 30–45 minutes on a rack.
summary: Banana, oat and apple loaf baked on the rice cooker Cake setting.
time: 15 min preparation plus one Cake cycle and extra time if needed
title: Rice cooker banana oat and apple loaf

ingredients.item: Thyme, nutmeg or mild curry powder
Pumpkin seeds or croutons to serve

proTips: Start with less stock; you can add liquid easily but cannot remove it without further cooking.
Blend very thoroughly for restaurant texture.
steps: Heat oven to 220°C conventional or 200°C fan. Toss butternut, onion and garlic with oil and seasoning. Spread on a tray and roast 30–40 minutes until soft with browned edges.
Squeeze garlic from skins. Put roasted vegetables in a pot, add 750 ml stock and optional herbs or spice. Simmer 10–15 minutes.
Remove herb stalks and blend until completely smooth, adding remaining stock to reach a thick but pourable texture.
Stir in cream if using and warm gently. Balance salt, pepper and a little lemon or vinegar. Serve with toasted seeds, a cream swirl or croutons.
summary: Roasted butternut blended smooth with stock and a little cream.
time: 15 min preparation plus 45–55 min cooking
title: Roasted butternut soup

proTips: Rest the lamb a full 15–20 minutes; the juices settle and the slices stay pink and moist.
Carve across the grain in thin slices.
steps: Heat to 220°C conventional or 200°C fan. Pat lamb dry, lightly score a thick fat layer without cutting deeply, and rub with oil, rosemary and moderate salt and pepper.
Roast fat side upwards for 20 minutes. Reduce to 160°C conventional or 145–150°C fan and continue. Begin checking the thickest part early rather than relying on weight alone.
Lay bacon loosely over the lamb for the final 25–30 minutes. For the conservative whole-cut endpoint used here, reach 63°C and rest at least 3 minutes; allow 15–20 minutes for a joint.
Roast cubed sweet potato and butternut separately at 200°C conventional or 180°C fan for 30–40 minutes, turning once. If sharing the cooler oven, allow longer and finish hotter while lamb rests.
Slice lamb, chop crisp bacon over the top and serve with roots and a squeeze of lemon.
summary: Rosemary lamb roast finished under bacon, with roasted sweet potato and butternut.
time: 25 min preparation plus roughly 80–110 min roasting and 20 min rest
tips: A 1.7 kg joint of leg is ideal; a shoulder needs a long braise instead.
title: Rosemary lamb with bacon and roasted roots

ingredients.item: medium apples, peeled and sliced about 2 mm thick

proTips: Mixing sweet and tart apples adds interest.
A mandoline gives even slices but use its guard.
The cake should contain much more apple than batter.
steps: Heat to 180°C conventional or 160°C fan. Grease and line a small cake tin, approximately 18–20 cm as a working size. Prepare thin apple slices.
Whisk eggs and sugar until slightly pale and fluffy. Mix in milk, melted butter and vanilla.
Combine flour, baking powder, salt and optional cinnamon, then fold into the wet mixture just until smooth.
Fold in apples, coating every slice. Transfer to tin and settle the layers. Keep below about three quarters full; bake any excess separately.
Bake about 40–50 minutes until golden and set in the middle with no liquid batter. Cool in tin 10–15 minutes before turning out. Serve warm with custard or cool for neater slices.
summary: Thinly sliced apples held together by a little vanilla batter. A family keeper.
time: 15 min preparation plus 40–50 min baking
tips: Two 12 cm cakes: 3 apples, 2 eggs, 70–80 g sugar, 120 ml milk, 80 g flour, 20 g butter, 5 ml each vanilla and baking powder, salt. Divide between sufficiently deep tins and bake about 30–40 min at 180°C conventional. Lighter full version: 60 g sugar, 80 g flour and 15 g butter; other ingredients unchanged.
title: Rustic sliced apple cake

ingredients.item: skinless salmon, in one piece or four portions
frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

proTips: Dry spinach and salmon protect the pastry.
steps: Soften finely chopped shallot in butter. Add garlic and dry spinach, stirring until all excess moisture has gone. Cool fully.
Mix spinach with cream cheese, Dijon, zest and dill. Dry and season salmon.
Put cold pastry on a lined tray. Spread a thin layer of spinach filling, add salmon and the remaining filling, then wrap, sealing seam underneath without excessive overlapping dough.
Chill briefly, egg wash and cut vents. Bake at 200°C conventional or 180°C fan for about 25–35 minutes, longer for a thick whole parcel.
Check the salmon centre reaches 63°C and pastry is deeply golden. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.
summary: Salmon on spinach and lemon cream cheese, wrapped in puff pastry.
time: 30 min preparation plus chilling and 25–35 min baking
tips: Quick version for two: 2 salmon fillets (150 g each), 320 g puff pastry, 100 g cream cheese mixed with 1 grated garlic clove, lemon zest and 10 g chopped dill. Bake 22–25 minutes at 180°C fan.
title: Salmon Wellington with spinach

proTips: Take the caramel genuinely dark, just short of acrid; that is where the flavour lives.
Stop whipping while the cream still flops over slightly. Overwhipped cream turns grainy, and warm custard knocks out the air.
steps: Make the fudge swirl: melt the butter with the brown sugar and golden syrup over low heat, stir in the cream and simmer gently 3–4 minutes until glossy. Add the salt, pour into a jar and cool completely. It should stay pourable.
Heat the milk and 250 ml cream until steaming, not boiling. Keep warm.
In a dry, heavy pan, heat the sugar and water without stirring, just swirling the pan, until it turns deep amber and smells toasty. Watch closely at the end.
Off the heat, pour the warm dairy into the caramel a little at a time, whisking. It hisses and bubbles hard, so stand back. Whisk smooth.

Whisk the yolks in a bowl, whisk in a ladle of the hot caramel cream, then pour it all back into the pan. Cook on low, stirring constantly, until it coats the back of a spoon at about 82°C. Do not let it boil.
Strain, stir in the vanilla and salt, cover and chill until fridge-cold, ideally overnight.
In the stand mixer, whip the 300 ml cold cream to soft peaks only. Fold in the cold custard in two or three additions by hand.
Layer a third into a freezer box, drizzle with fudge swirl and repeat. Drag a knife through once or twice, then freeze at least 6 hours.
summary: Burnt-caramel custard folded into whipped cream with a chewy fudge ribble. No ice cream machine needed.
time: 45 min active plus overnight chilling and 6 hours freezing
tips: South African shortcut: warmed Caramel Treat works in place of the homemade fudge swirl.
For properly salted caramel, raise the salt in the custard to 3–4 g and taste it cold before folding.
title: No-churn salted caramel fudge ice cream

ingredients.item: chicken stock, enough for a shallow layer
crushed garlic cloves and 2 thyme sprigs
butter and 5 ml lemon juice for sauce

proTips: Keep the shallow stock below most of the browned surface.
Remove smaller breasts as they finish.
steps: Heat oven to 180°C conventional or 160–170°C fan. Dry chicken and season. Heat an ovenproof cast iron pan with oil.
Brown breasts for around 2–3 minutes per side, in batches if necessary. Add stock and optional aromatics around them.

Cover tightly with foil and move to the oven. Start checking after 10 minutes if thoroughly seared, or 15 minutes for thick breasts. Continue as needed until each breast reaches 74°C in its thickest part.
Rest for 5–8 minutes. Reduce pan juices briefly; finish with butter and lemon if desired. Slice just before serving.
summary: Golden-seared chicken breasts finished covered in a little stock so they stay juicy.
time: 15 min preparation plus roughly 10–22 min oven cooking and 5–8 min rest
title: Seared chicken breasts finished in stock

proTips: Use the paddle briefly rather than the dough hook; overmixing develops toughness.
Blind bake a base when the filling is very wet.
servesLabel: Base and lid for a 23 cm pie
steps: Mix flour and salt. Rub in cold butter with fingertips or pulse briefly with the mixer paddle on low until coarse crumbs remain.
Add 60 ml water and gently bring together. Add more 5 ml at a time, only until it holds when pressed. Do not knead.
Flatten into two discs, wrap and chill at least 30 minutes.
Roll 3 mm thick on a lightly floured surface. Line a pie dish without stretching, add cold cooked filling and fit the lid. Crimp, vent and glaze.
Bake according to the filling recipe, generally in a 200°C conventional or 180°C fan oven until pastry is cooked and golden and the filling is fully hot.
summary: A reliable all-butter shortcrust for the base and lid of a savoury pie.
time: 15 min preparation plus at least 30 min chilling
title: Shortcrust pastry for a savoury pie

ingredients.item: Bay leaf and half a garlic clove
Salt, pepper, lemon and 5 ml olive oil to finish

proTips: No soaking is normally needed.
steps: Pick over and rinse lentils. Put in a saucepan with water and optional aromatics.
Bring to a simmer and cook gently, usually 20–30 minutes for green or brown lentils, until tender but intact. Add water if needed.
Drain excess liquid, remove bay and season with salt, pepper, lemon and oil.
For red split lentils, begin checking after 10–15 minutes; they break down and are better for a soft purée or soup.
summary: Simple seasoned lentils for one, easy to scale up.
time: 5 min preparation plus 15–30 min cooking
title: Simple cooked lentils
