ingredients.item: –1.2 litres beef stock, including replacement for omitted wine
Puff pastry to cover a large deep dish

proTips: Replace wine with equal stock; finish with a little Worcestershire or vinegar if needed.
Make the filling the day before and bake the lid fresh.
steps: Dry and season beef. Brown in batches in hot oil, then reserve. Soften onions and carrots in the same pot. Add garlic for 30 seconds and tomato paste for 1–2 minutes.
Stir in flour for 1 minute. Add stock gradually, scraping the pot, followed by Worcestershire, thyme and bay. Return beef.
Simmer very gently, partly covered, for around 2½–3½ hours until spoon tender. Stir occasionally and replace evaporated liquid as needed.
Add potatoes for the final 25–30 minutes. Reduce until gravy coats the pieces and a spoon trail closes slowly. Remove bay and adjust seasoning.
Divide into shallow containers, cool promptly and refrigerate. Assemble with fully cold filling in a large dish. Fit one pastry lid, crimp, cut vents and brush with egg.
Bake at 200°C conventional or 180°C fan for approximately 35–45 minutes, until deeply golden and the centre of the filling reaches 74°C. Rest 10 minutes.
summary: Spoon-tender beef and potato braise under one golden puff pastry lid.
time: 35 min preparation plus 3–4 hours braising, chilling and 35–45 min baking
tips: For the original smaller 4–6 portion version use 1.2–1.3 kg beef, 1 onion, 2 carrots, 2 garlic cloves, 30 ml each tomato paste and flour, 650 ml total stock, 5–10 ml Worcestershire, 2.5 ml dried thyme, 1 bay and 2–3 potatoes.
title: Slow braised beef and potato pie

ingredients.item: medium potato or sweet potato, diced

proTips: Use canned or already safely cooked beans, not raw dried kidney beans.
steps: Put all ingredients except leafy greens and final seasoning into the slow cooker. Stir and cover.
Cook on low for 7–8 hours or high for 4–5 hours, until root vegetables are tender. Keep courgette chunks large, or add them for the last hour for more texture.
Add greens for the final 20–30 minutes. Mash a ladleful of beans and vegetables into the broth for body.
Taste, adjust salt and pepper and serve. Add parsley or Parmesan if desired.
summary: Beans and garden vegetables left to simmer all day in the slow cooker.
time: 15 min preparation plus 7–8 hours low or 4–5 hours high
title: Slow cooker vegetable and bean soup

Use soft butter, not melted butter, in this recipe.
steps: Heat to 175°C conventional or 160°C fan. Grease and line a 15–16 cm round tin. Mash banana.
Cream butter and sugar until pale. Beat in egg and vanilla, adding 5 ml of the flour if it starts to split.
Fold in flour, baking powder, salt and optional cinnamon, then banana and milk. Batter should drop softly from a spoon.
Bake 28–35 minutes, checking from 28, until a skewer has moist crumbs without raw batter.
Rest 10 minutes in tin, then turn out. Serve warm with the small batch custard.
summary: A small, soft banana sponge for an afternoon treat.
time: 15 min preparation plus 28–35 min baking
title: Small banana sponge cake

proTips: For a vegetarian guest, use cheeses made with vegetarian rennet.
A sensible schedule is lasagna at minute 0, Wellingtons around minute 25–30, lasagna out around 45 and rested while chicken finishes; temperature checks take priority.
steps: Chop vegetables. Soften onion in oil, brown mushrooms, then add garlic, courgette, pepper and carrot. Add tomato paste, tomatoes and herbs; simmer 10–15 minutes until thick. Stir in spinach and season.
Melt butter, cook flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in milk. Simmer until thick. Add salt, pepper, nutmeg and 50 g cheese off the heat.
In a deep 20 cm dish, layer a little vegetable sauce, pasta, vegetables, cheese sauce and optional ricotta. Repeat. Finish with white sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan style cheese.
Bake at 180°C fan for about 30–40 minutes freshly assembled, or 40–50 minutes from chilled, following pasta directions. Cover if browning early and check the centre reaches 74°C.
Rest 15 minutes before slicing.
summary: Vegetable ragu and cheese sauce layered with pasta for two or three.
time: 35 min preparation plus 35–45 min baking and 15 min rest
title: Small vegetarian birthday lasagna

steps: Heat to 190°C conventional or 170°C fan. Grease and line a 22–23 cm round tin.
Cream butter and sugar for 3–4 minutes until pale. Beat in eggs one at a time, followed by vanilla and optional oil.
Mix flour, baking powder and salt. Fold in half, then half the milk, and repeat. Stop when combined.
Bake 25–30 minutes, checking at 24–25, until springy and a skewer emerges without wet batter.
Leave in tin 10 minutes, then turn out and serve warm with custard.
summary: A soft vanilla sponge made to be served warm with custard.
time: 15 min preparation plus 25–30 min baking
title: Soft vanilla sponge for warm custard

proTips: Knead until a small piece stretches thin without tearing; wholemeal needs a little longer than white.
Brush with butter straight out of the oven for a soft crust.
steps: Mix flours, yeast and salt. Add water, oil and honey. Knead 8–10 minutes until elastic; wholemeal dough can remain slightly tacky.
Cover and let rise until roughly doubled, about 60–90 minutes.
Shape into a log and put in a greased loaf tin. Cover and proof 40–60 minutes until puffy.
Bake at 200°C conventional or 180°C fan for 30–40 minutes until well browned and the base is firm. Remove from tin and cool fully on a rack.
summary: A soft everyday sandwich loaf with 40% wholemeal flour.
time: 25 min preparation plus 1½–2½ hours rising and 30–40 min baking
title: Soft wholemeal sandwich loaf

proTips: For make ahead, chill promptly and reheat covered until hot through.
Half all quantities for one dish.
servesLabel: Two large dishes or about 20 portions
steps: Heat to 180°C conventional or 160°C fan. Butter two large 24–26 cm dishes with enough depth for expansion; batter should not exceed roughly two thirds of each dish.
Beat eggs and sugar until pale. Mix in apricot jam. Have flour and salt combined, and milk lukewarm.
Stir bicarbonate into milk, then vinegar. Immediately alternate the milk mixture and flour into the eggs. Fold in cooled melted butter and divide between dishes.
Bake around 40–45 minutes in moderate-depth dishes, or 50–60 minutes or more for a deep pudding. Check the centre for cooked moist crumbs, not liquid batter. Tent if top browns early.
Meanwhile gently boil sauce ingredients except vanilla for 5–7 minutes, stirring. Remove from heat and add vanilla.
Pierce the hot baked puddings deeply. Reheat sauce if necessary and pour half slowly over each, pausing to absorb. Leave 15–20 minutes before serving with custard.
summary: Spongy apricot pudding soaked in a rich cream and butter sauce. Makes two big dishes.
time: 25 min preparation plus 40–60 min baking and 20 min soaking
title: South African malva pudding (two large dishes)

steps: Mix pastry dry ingredients, rub in cold butter and gently bind with egg. Chill 15–30 minutes. Roll about 3 mm thick, line a 24 cm tart dish and chill again.
Bake at 170°C conventional with paper and weights for 12 minutes; remove weights and bake about 12 minutes more until cooked and golden.

Whisk filling ingredients smooth while cold, dissolving cornflour in the extra liquid first. Heat slowly, whisking continuously, until thick with gentle bubbles; continue whisking briefly to cook the starch.
Fill the shell, dust with cinnamon and refrigerate promptly. Chill at least 6 hours, preferably overnight.
summary: Melktert: a crisp sweet crust and a silky set milk custard dusted with cinnamon.
time: 35 min preparation plus about 24 min pastry baking and at least 6 hours chilling
title: South African milk tart

ingredients.item: beef stock, plus extra if needed
puff pastry, with extra if your tins require it
egg and 15 ml milk for glazing

proTips: Bake on a preheated heavy tray for a crisp base.
The filling should mound when cold.
For freezing, freeze assembled unbaked pies on a tray, bag when firm, and bake from frozen with additional time; verify the centre, not just the pastry.
steps: Dry beef and brown in 3–4 batches in hot oil. Reserve. Cook onion in the pot for 6–8 minutes and garlic for 30 seconds.

Stir in tomato paste and flour for 1–2 minutes. Add Worcestershire, soy and stock gradually, scraping the base. Add Dijon, thyme, sugar, 10 ml cracked pepper and the ground pepper. Return beef and juices.
Cover and simmer gently for about 1½–2½ hours, until tender but still in pieces. Add stock if drying. Uncover and reduce 10–20 minutes until very thick.
Stir in remaining cracked pepper to taste and butter. Season carefully because stock and soy are salty. Cool promptly in a shallow dish and refrigerate until fully cold, preferably overnight.
Grease eight 10–12 cm pie tins. Roll pastry to about 3 mm. Line without stretching, fill to 5–8 mm below the rim and seal pastry lids with a little egg wash. Crimp and vent.

Chill 15–20 minutes. Apply two thin egg washes, keeping cut edges clear. Bake at 200°C fan for 10 minutes, then 180°C fan for 20–25 minutes or longer until bases are crisp and filling reaches 74°C. Rest 10–15 minutes.
summary: Individual peppery beef pies, the South African bakery classic.
time: 35 min preparation plus 2–3 hours cooking, chilling and 30–40 min baking
title: South African pepper steak pies

proTips: Drain the pumpkin before adding flour; excess flour makes heavy fritters.
steps: Steam or boil pumpkin until tender. Drain very thoroughly, mash and cool. If watery, stir briefly over low heat to dry, then cool again.
Mix in egg, sugar, salt and cinnamon. Fold in flour and baking powder to make a soft spoonable batter. Add 15 ml or two of flour only if needed.
Heat a shallow layer of oil over medium heat, around 170–175°C if measuring. Fry a small test fritter.
Drop small spoonfuls, gently flatten and fry about 2–3 minutes per side until golden and cooked in the centre. Work in batches.
Drain briefly, then toss warm fritters in cinnamon sugar. Serve immediately.
summary: Pumpkin fritters fried golden and rolled in cinnamon sugar.
time: 20 min preparation plus cooling and 15–20 min frying
title: South African pumpkin fritters

proTips: Browning mince in two batches gives more flavour than steaming a crowded pan.
steps: Soften onion and optional carrot in oil for 8 minutes. Add garlic briefly.
Brown mince thoroughly, breaking up clumps, and cook to 71°C. Stir in tomato paste for 1–2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, stock and oregano. Simmer gently for 45–75 minutes, adding water if needed, until thick and rich.
Season and stir in basil. Cook pasta, reserve a little pasta water and toss pasta with some sauce before serving.
Top with remaining sauce and cheese.
summary: A slow-simmered beef and pork mince ragu over spaghetti.
time: 20 min preparation plus 45–75 min simmering
title: Spaghetti Bolognese

proTips: The riper the bananas the better: black-speckled skins give the most flavour, so you can cut the sugar to 100 g.
Stop the mixer the moment the flour disappears; overmixing makes a tough, dense loaf.
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease a 23 × 13 cm loaf tin or two 12 cm round tins.
Mash the bananas in the mixer bowl with the flat beater on low for 30–60 seconds.
With the mixer on low, add the melted butter, both sugars and the egg. Mix until just combined.
Add the bicarbonate, salt, cinnamon and flour. Mix on low only until no dry flour remains, about 30 seconds.
Bake a loaf tin for 55–65 minutes, or two 12 cm tins for 35–50 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then turn out onto a rack.
summary: The simple banana bread first made in the new mixer. One batch fills two 12 cm tins.
time: 10 min preparation plus 35–65 min baking
tips: Two 12 cm tins need the full batch. Two-thirds less was nowhere near enough.
No vanilla extract? Swap 15 g of the sugar for vanilla sugar, as here.
Great for a picnic with butter and jam, or whipped cream and jam.
title: Stand mixer banana bread

proTips: A grill adds browning, not true smoke flavour.
steps: Remove the membrane from the bone side if present. Dry ribs, press on rub and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or overnight.
Heat to 135°C conventional or about 120°C fan. Put ribs bone side down on a rack over a lined tray and tightly cover the whole tray with foil.
Cook roughly 2½–3½ hours, until a probe slides into the meat easily and the rack bends readily; tenderness commonly comes around 88–95°C, well above the safety minimum.
Uncover for the final 20–30 minutes and brush with BBQ sauce several times. Finish briefly under a watched grill for a sticky crust.
Rest 10 minutes and cut between bones.
summary: Rubbed spare ribs cooked covered in a low oven, then glazed sticky with BBQ sauce.
time: 20 min preparation plus 2½–3½ hours cooking
title: Sticky oven barbecue spare ribs

proTips: This is a date-free toffee sponge, not the fruit-based traditional sticky toffee formula.
It was offered as an alternative, with approximate metric conversions supplied here.
steps: Heat to 180°C conventional or 160°C fan. Grease a medium baking dish.
Cream butter and sugar. Beat in eggs one at a time. Fold in flour and baking powder alternately with milk and vanilla.
Bake 30–40 minutes until the centre is set and a skewer shows cooked crumbs.
Simmer sauce ingredients gently for 5 minutes. Poke the hot cake and pour hot sauce over gradually.
Rest 10–15 minutes to absorb before serving.
summary: Brown sugar sponge with a warm toffee sauce, no dates needed.
time: 20 min preparation plus 30–40 min baking
title: Sticky toffee style pudding without dates

proTips: The batter is supposed to pour easily.
Rest before deciding it needs more flour.
The first pancake is a useful heat and consistency test.
steps: Mix flour and salt. Whisk in about half the milk to a smooth paste. Add eggs, remaining milk, melted butter or oil and optional flavouring.
Rest 20–30 minutes. Use 500 ml for the slightly thicker version you preferred, adding more milk if needed.
Heat a lightly greased nonstick pan over medium to medium high heat. Add a thin layer of batter and swirl immediately.
Cook 1–2 minutes until the edge lifts and the base is golden. Flip and cook 30–60 seconds more.
Keep a short stack warm and serve with jam and cream, berries, lemon sugar or cinnamon sugar.
summary: Thin Swedish pannkakor, lovely with jam and cream.
time: 10 min preparation plus 20–30 min rest and 20 min frying
title: Swedish thin pancakes

proTips: Lower heat gives thick centres time to cook before the surface burns.
For the small four-pancake version, use 125 g flour, 10 ml baking powder, 15 ml sugar, 1.25 ml salt, 1 egg, 180 ml milk and 30 ml melted butter.
steps: Mix flour, baking powder, sugar and salt. Whisk eggs, 250 ml milk, butter or oil and vanilla separately.
Fold wet into dry just until combined. Keep a few small lumps. Rest 10 minutes.
The batter should fall in heavy ribbons. Add remaining milk only if needed.
Cook 30–45 ml portions in a lightly greased pan over medium low heat. Flip once bubbles appear and edges set, then cook 1–2 minutes on the other side.
Check the first one is cooked through and adjust heat before cooking the batch.
summary: Thick, fluffy South African flapjacks for a weekend breakfast.
time: 10 min mixing plus 10 min rest and 15–20 min cooking
title: Thick fluffy flapjacks

ingredients.item: salt, pepper and thyme or rosemary

proTips: Blending only half retains some vegetable texture.
steps: Soften chopped onion and celery in oil. Add garlic, pumpkin, courgettes and sweet potato and stir for 5 minutes.
Add enough stock to just cover, reserving the rest. Simmer gently for 20–25 minutes until the sweet potato and pumpkin are tender.
Stir in spinach for 3–5 minutes. Remove woody herb stems and blend all or part of the soup.
Adjust thickness with reserved stock and season. Serve with bread and, optionally, a little sour cream.
summary: A thick, chunky soup of pumpkin, sweet potato, courgette and spinach.
time: 15 min preparation plus 30 min cooking
title: Thick pumpkin sweet potato and spinach soup

proTips: An earlier structured variation added 1 egg, used 60 ml cocoa and optional 30 g flour; if choosing it, bake until the egg-containing centre is cooked through.
steps: Heat to 175°C conventional or 160°C fan. Line a small shallow tin, roughly 15–18 cm square as a working size.
Mix banana, peanut butter and cocoa thoroughly. Spread evenly in the tin.
Bake 20–25 minutes until the centre is set rather than fluid. These remain dense and soft.
Cool completely before slicing; chilling gives firmer squares.
summary: Banana, peanut butter and cocoa. That is the whole recipe.
time: 10 min preparation plus 20–25 min baking and cooling
title: Three ingredient banana peanut butter brownies

proTips: Steam drying the potatoes is the difference between fluffy mash and a watery topping.
steps: Heat to 200°C fan. Boil potatoes in salted water for 15–20 minutes until tender.
Soften onion and carrot in butter for 6–8 minutes. Stir in flour for 1 minute, then gradually add milk and simmer until thick.
Add mustard, peas, corn and herbs; cook 2–3 minutes. Fold in tuna off the heat, then lemon and seasoning. Put in a deep 23 cm dish or a larger dish if needed.
Drain potatoes and steam dry 2–3 minutes. Mash with warmed milk and butter. Spoon over from the edges towards the centre and roughen with a fork.
Add optional cheese. Bake 25–30 minutes until bubbling and 74°C in the middle. Grill briefly for colour if needed; rest 5 minutes.
summary: Creamy tuna and vegetable filling topped with fluffy mash and baked golden.
time: 30 min preparation plus 25–30 min baking
title: Tuna cottage pie

ingredients.item: puff pastry sheets, enough for two 20 cm squares after shrinkage
vanilla extract or about 15 ml vanilla sugar

proTips: Do not reduce the cornflour: this filling must slice rather than pour.
Buy pastry by usable area as well as weight.
A deep golden bake helps it stay crisp longer.
steps: Heat to 200°C fan. Cut pastry slightly oversize. Bake each sheet between baking paper with a second tray on top for 15–25 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Cool; trim to fit the lined tin.
Heat 600 ml milk with half the sugar. Whisk remaining milk, yolks, remaining sugar, cornflour, salt and vanilla sugar if using until smooth.
Temper with hot milk, return to saucepan and whisk over moderate low heat until very thick. Once gently bubbling, cook another 60–90 seconds. Remove and whisk in butter and vanilla extract.

Spread hot custard over the bottom pastry. Fit the top gently. For easy portions, cut the top sheet into rectangles before assembly. Cool promptly and refrigerate at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Mix icing ingredients to a thick spreadable consistency, spread over cold pastry and chill 20–30 minutes. Saw gently through the top with a serrated knife, then cut down through the custard.
summary: Thick vanilla custard set between puff pastry with a white icing top.
time: 35 min preparation plus 15–25 min pastry baking and overnight chilling
title: Vanilla custard slices

proTips: These are starch-thickened custards, which need a brief gentle bubble to cook the starch.
Pure egg custard without starch needs different heat control.
Vanilla sugar adds sweetness as well as flavour; start low.
Flour is not an equal weight substitute for cornflour.
steps: Choose one formula. Reserve some cold milk and heat the remainder until steaming. Whisk cold milk, cornflour, sugar, salt and yolks if used to a smooth paste.
Gradually whisk hot milk into the paste. Return everything to the saucepan.

Cook over medium low heat, whisking and scraping the corners. Once thick and gently bubbling, continue briefly, usually about 1 minute for the smaller rich batches or 2–3 minutes for the litre batch, without a violent boil.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla and butter. If using vanilla sugar, include it with the sugar and adjust sweetness after cooking.
Serve warm. If holding, cover the surface to prevent a skin; cool promptly and refrigerate. Rewarm gently, whisking in milk if too thick.
summary: Smooth vanilla custard on the hob, with batch sizes for every pudding.
tips: Small batch: 300 ml milk, 2 yolks, 30 g sugar, 15 g cornflour, 5 ml vanilla, pinch of salt, optional 10 g butter.
Vanilla sugar batch: 400 ml milk, 3 yolks, 12–15 g cornflour, 30 ml sugar, 10–15 ml vanilla sugar and salt.
Lighter large batch: 1 litre milk, 35–40 g cornflour, 60 ml sugar, 10 ml vanilla, salt, and optional 2 yolks and 20 g butter.
title: Vanilla custard

proTips: Cycle duration depends on the appliance; a finished programme alone does not prove the centre is baked.
steps: Grease the rice cooker bowl. Cream butter and sugar for 3–4 minutes. Beat in eggs one at a time, then vanilla.
Combine flour, baking powder and salt. Fold into butter mixture alternately with milk, mixing only until combined.
Put into bowl within your model Cake capacity and smooth the top. Select Cake.
At cycle completion, test the centre. If there is wet batter, continue for 10–20 minutes using the model controls and check again.
Rest in switched-off bowl 10 minutes, turn out and cool on a rack.
summary: A buttery vanilla sponge baked in the Yum Asia rice cooker.
time: 15 min preparation plus Cake cycle, usually around 50–60 min with further checks
tips: Fluffier egg-white version for the Samura Cake setting: whisk 3 egg whites to soft peaks, add 90 g caster sugar to firm peaks, whisk in the 3 yolks and 2.5 ml vanilla, fold in 90 g self-raising flour then 20 g melted butter. Cake setting about 50 minutes, check at 40, then rest 15–20 minutes with the lid closed.
title: Vanilla sponge in the Yum Asia Sakura

ingredients.item: wholemeal flour or 35 g wheat bran plus 25 g plain flour

proTips: Pure stevia is not a gram-for-gram sugar replacement.
steps: Heat to 175°C conventional or 160°C fan and line a loaf tin.
Mash bananas and mix in butter, sugar, egg and vanilla.
Combine flours or bran blend with bicarbonate and salt, then fold into wet mixture. Add nuts or seeds if using.
Bake 50–60 minutes, checking for a set centre without raw batter. Tent if browning early.
Cool in tin 10 minutes, then on a rack.
summary: A less sweet banana loaf with wholemeal flour or wheat bran.
time: 15 min preparation plus 50–60 min baking
title: Wholemeal banana and bran loaf
